sources.journal: user lsi, PID 505510, 2026-10-28 12:45–13:05 local session window

confirmed_evidence.fact: Kicker opens a child dialog after hover delay, clears hide-on-deactivate while focus transfers, calls windowSystem.forceActive(childDialog.mainItem), then sets mainItem.focus=true.
A submenu window deactivation closes the whole Kicker menu unless the dialog is being destroyed.

During menu activity on the Wayland session there are KX11Extras::forceActiveWindow X11-only warnings, ItemListDialog shadow recreation warnings and eglSwapBuffers surface 0x0 warnings. They are correlated with menu activity but do not prove the cause of the reported closure or restart.
An application is launched on pointer release and closes the menu; pointer exit itself only clears press state and stops the timer. This does not explain a Plasma restart on double-click.
No plasmashell coredump after 2026-10-26; the current PID has no fatal record in the inspected interval.

interpretation: A possible hover-close chain is Kicker opening a submenu, attempting focus transfer through its WindowSystem, then the submenu receiving a deactivation signal and setting kicker.expanded=false. The Wayland warnings support investigating this path, but no stack/event trace proves causality. R593 window focus correction remains a candidate; it has not been loaded/tested live.
action: No additional code change: the implicated WindowSystem.forceActive call and ItemListDialog deactivation handler are KDE-owned source loaded from /usr/share, not code in this theme repository. Avoid copying/forking KDE implementation without a controlled proof and scope decision.
next: Safely reload and test R593 in the current lsi session when there is a maintenance window, then observe whether moving over a top-level category spawns a submenu and closes the parent.
If it persists, isolate the popup/Wayland activation path before considering a KDE QML compatibility adaptation.
Wait for Q510 to identify affected apps and distinguish app launch stall from plasmashell restart.
